messages:
ash: Getting alerts — eu3 egress is saturated, packet retransmit and queue growth on the gpu fabric. Inference tail latencies climbing to ~2.4s for long sequences. 1/3 of requests are seeing dropped frames.
incident-bot: ALERT: region=eu3 severity=P2 service=inference-runtime description=egress_degradation paging=oncall (ops-rotation)
ash: I already scoped: it's not control-plane, looks like an ISP peering flap hitting our eu3 egress NATs. GPU pools are healthy but traffic is stalling in the network layer.
maria: Copy. Any immediate mitigation options? Can we shift traffic temporarily?
ash: Yes — plan A: shift 60% of inference traffic off eu3 to eu1/eu2 routing layer and set fallback to small-quantized model to reduce bandwidth. Running canary now.
ash: Executing reroute (canary):
```bash
rbox route shift --from eu3 --to eu1,eu2 --service inference-api --percent 20 --type canary
```
deploy-bot: Started route-shift canary job 0a3f. Canary 20% -> eu1,eu2. Monitoring latency and error-rate for 5m.
kevin: If canary looks good, push to 60% then 100% gradual. Ops note: shifting increases cross-region egress costs, escrow estimate +$3.5k/day at peak.
sre-lead: Agree on staged ramp. Also we need to tweak incident-bot escalation to avoid duplicate pages from transient net flaps — let's reduce duplicate noise so oncall can focus.
maria: What change do you propose?
sre-lead: Two tweaks: 1) debounce identical egress alerts for 8m; 2) widen first-escalation window to 12m before paging secondary. Keeps primary engaged but prevents immediate loud escalation for known transients.
ash: Can you gate that change? We should add label-based suppression for scheduled maintenance too (we're seeing noisy alerts even for planned network tests).
sre-lead: Patching incident-bot config now:
```yaml
incident_bot:
  dedupe_period: 8m
  escalation:
    primary_delay: 0m
    secondary_delay: 12m
  suppress_if:
    - label: maintenance
      action: suppress
```
incident-bot: CONFIG UPDATE applied by sre-lead. dedupe_period=8m secondary_delay=12m suppression_labels=[maintenance]
ops-rotation: Oncall acknowledged. I'm keeping the war room open and watching the canary.
maria: Canary telemetry: error-rate down from 12% to 4% in eu1, latency stable. No service errors yet. Recommend ramp to 60%.
ash: Ramp to 60% now:
```bash
rbox route shift --from eu3 --to eu1,eu2 --service inference-api --percent 60 --fast-failover true
```
deploy-bot: Route-shift job 0a3f -> 60% applied. Observability link: https://console.redwood/obs/route/0a3f
kevin: Cost callout: 60% shift will create ~1.8TB/day inter-region egress. We can enable KV caching + prefix caching to reduce repeat tokens; recommend enabling short TTL cache for common prefixes during shift.
ash: Enabled prefix cache rule for inference-api: ttl=30s scope=global.
sre-lead: Good. Also, ops, start provisioning two extra low-priority GPU nodes in eu1 as temporary capacity buffer in case load spikes. We have reserved quota but need quick spin-up.
ops-rotation: Spinning up 2x A10s low-priority in eu1 now. ETA 7m.
maria: We should also patch routing policy to prefer local model quantized fallback when cross-region latency > 180ms to minimize token churn. Adding rule:
```json
{
  "route_policy": "latency_pref_local",
  "threshold_ms": 180,
  "fallback": "quantized-1.5b"
}
```
ash: Applied. That will reduce egress for heavy requests.
kevin: Quick cost trade: hot-standby (reserved) vs burst-on-demand — hot-standby increases monthly fixed cost but reduces failover risk. For months with spikes, hot-standby might be cheaper than sustained egress. Filing a short analysis doc after incident.
sre-lead: Ops, remind next oncall to verify incident-bot metrics and revert dedupe back to default after we confirm root cause? We don't want longer suppression permanently.
ops-rotation: Noted. I'll add an automated follow-up task to the incident timeline to review dedupe after RCA.
ash: RCA in progress — working with transit provider for packet captures. Early suspicion: BGP flap on one transit peer causing asymmetric routing and re-queuing in our egress NAT cluster.
maria: Any customer-facing comms needed? Are SLOs breached?
sre-lead: We'll hold on broad comms — this is P2, degradation in a subset of eu3 customers only. If we ramp again or see persistent errors, draft status update.
ops-rotation: Handoff checklist for next oncall (copying here so it's on thread): 1) Check incident-bot dedupe and escalation status. 2) Confirm route-shift percent and any scheduled reroutes. 3) Verify temp GPUs health in eu1. 4) Confirm caching TTL rules active. 5) Follow provider updates for BGP.
ash: Adding final note: After eu3 stabilizes, we should revert route-shift in reverse order and revoke extra GPUs to avoid ongoing cost. Plan a 1:1 with networking to evaluate longer-term peering fixes and potential purchase of additional peering capacity.
kevin: I'll queue the cost analysis and recommend capacity option in ~24h.
ops-rotation: Handing off to @maria for next shift in 12m. Leaving war room open.
maria: Ack, taking over. I'll post a short handoff summary and close when eu3 shows healthy metrics for 30m with stable error-rate <1%. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: previous alerts deduped and escalation adjusted. Timeline updated.
